question: The pie charts below show exports from various EU countries to India and China in 2005 and 2015.
essay:
The given pie charts compare the changes in exports from EU countries to India and China between 2005 and 2015.

Overall, Germany emerged as the major exporter to both India and China, while shares of other countries either declined or remained unchanged.

Turning first to India, in 2005, the biggest exporter was the UK, 29%, followed by Belgium, 25%, and Germany, 15%. While in China, the exports from Germany were dominant, 38% and far exceeded that from France, 13%. In contrast, other nations accounted for less than 10% of exports' proportions to both countries.

Over a period of a decade, from 2005 to 2015, the exports patterns in India experienced a dramatic change, since the share of the UK halved to 13% and that of Belgium also fell by 5%. Whereas, Germany became the main exporter, at 25%. Exports from other countries remained stable.

Looking next at China, a 10-year period didn't witness much change in the exports' patterns, other than the proportion of Germany rising significantly from 38% to 48% and that of France decreased to 10%.
